speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing acute diarrhea; how long have your symptoms been present, and have you had any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection. Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia, followed by the onset of frequent watery diarrhea and cramping, this is highly suggestive of C. diff. I need to confirm this with a stool test for C. difficile toxin.

REQUEST TEST: Stool_C_diff_toxin
